subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: What proof is sufficient before changing or closing the OpenAI-to-Twilio realtime output clipping report?
rationale: The current source shows plausible codec and pacing boundaries, but automation cannot safely choose gain, provider format, pacer, or diagnostic behavior without live telephony evidence from the affected path.

options.title: Require live output evidence first
options.body: Collect a redacted current-main Twilio/OpenAI outbound-call repro with audio or queue/level logs before choosing the fix boundary.

options.title: Approve a narrow diagnostic patch
options.body: Allow a small maintainer-sponsored change that adds temporary peak, queue, and underrun logging for this path before audio behavior changes.

options.title: Close only after confirming adjacent fixes
options.body: If maintainers can live-verify that current main or a release no longer clips during startup, close this issue with that proof and release/commit provenance.

recommendation.title: Require live output evidence first
recommendation.body: Collect a redacted current-main Twilio/OpenAI outbound-call repro with audio or queue/level logs before choosing the fix boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent history on the shared audio codec and OpenAI realtime provider surfaces involved in the proof decision.
